passage:
Kevin bought shoes that made a squeaking sound on the school floor. Every step in the hallway sounded loud.
At first, his classmates laughed. Kevin tried to walk softly, but the shoes still squeaked.
The next day, he felt embarrassed and wanted to stay in the classroom. His friend said, "The sound is loud, but it is not you."
After a week, the sound became less noticeable. Other students stopped caring.
Kevin learned that embarrassment often feels larger to the person experiencing it than to everyone else. People may laugh for a moment and then move on.
The noisy shoes were uncomfortable, but they taught him that not every small problem deserves a whole day of worry.
